entries.pageContent: Physics Quick Notes — Basic Concepts  1. Physical Quantities  A   physical quantity   is anything that can be measured.  Examples: length, mass, time, temperature and speed.  Every physical quantity contains:  Physical quantity = Numerical value × Unit  Example:  Length = 5 metres  2. SI Base Units  Quantity   SI Unit   Symbol  Length   metre   m  Mass   kilogram   kg  Time   second   s  Temperature   kelvin   K  Electric current   ampere   A  Amount of  substance  mole   mol  Luminous intensity   candela   cd  3. Distance and Displacement  Distance  The total length of the path travelled by an object.  ●   Scalar quantity  ●   Has only magnitude  ●   Cannot be negative  ●   SI unit: metre  Displacement

The shortest straight-line distance from the initial position to the final position.  ●   Vector quantity  ●   Has magnitude and direction  ●   Can be positive, negative or zero  ●   SI unit: metre  Example:  A person walks 5 m forward and then 5 m backward.  ●   Distance = 10 m  ●   Displacement = 0 m  4. Speed and Velocity  Speed  Speed tells us how fast an object is moving.  [  \text{Speed}=\frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}}  ]  SI unit: metre per second, or m/s  Velocity  Velocity is the rate of change of displacement.  [  \text{Velocity}=\frac{\text{Displacement}}{\text{Time}}  ]  Velocity has both magnitude and direction.  Average Speed  [  \text{Average speed}=  \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}}  ]  5. Acceleration

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.  [  a=\frac{v-u}{t}  ]  Where:  ●   (a) = acceleration  ●   (u) = initial velocity  ●   (v) = final velocity  ●   (t) = time  SI unit: m/s²  Types of Acceleration  ●   Positive acceleration:   Velocity increases.  ●   Negative acceleration:   Velocity decreases.  ●   Zero acceleration:   Velocity remains constant.  Negative acceleration is also called   retardation   or   deceleration .  6. Equations of Motion  These equations are used when acceleration is constant.  [  v=u+at  ]  [  s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2  ]  [  v^2=u^2+2as  ]  Where:  ●   (u) = initial velocity  ●   (v) = final velocity  ●   (a) = acceleration  ●   (t) = time  ●   (s) = displacement

7. Force  Force is a push or pull that can change:  ●   The speed of an object  ●   The direction of motion  ●   The shape of an object  ●   The state of rest or motion  [  F=ma  ]  Where:  ●   (F) = force  ●   (m) = mass  ●   (a) = acceleration  SI unit: newton, or N  One newton is the force required to accelerate a mass of 1 kg at 1 m/s².  [  1N=1,kg,m/s^2  ]  8. Newton’s Laws of Motion  First Law  An object remains at rest or continues moving with constant velocity unless an external force acts on it.  This law is also called the   law of inertia .  Second Law  The acceleration produced in an object is directly proportional to the applied force and inversely proportional to its mass.  [  F=ma  ]

Third Law  For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.  Example: When a gun fires a bullet forward, the gun moves backward.  9. Mass and Weight  Mass  Mass is the amount of matter present in an object.  ●   Constant everywhere  ●   Scalar quantity  ●   SI unit: kilogram  Weight  Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object.  [  W=mg  ]  Where:  ●   (W) = weight  ●   (m) = mass  ●   (g) = acceleration due to gravity  On Earth:  [  g\approx9.8,m/s^2  ]  Weight is measured in newtons.  10. Momentum  Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.

[  p=mv  ]  SI unit:  [  kg,m/s  ]  A heavy or fast-moving object has greater momentum.  Conservation of Momentum  When no external force acts on a system:  [  \text{Total initial momentum}  \text{Total final momentum}  ]  11. Work  Work is done when a force moves an object through a certain distance.  [  W=Fs  ]  When force and displacement make an angle (\theta):  [  W=Fs\cos\theta  ]  SI unit: joule, or J  ●   Positive work: Force and displacement are in the same direction.  ●   Negative work: Force and displacement are in opposite directions.  ●   Zero work: There is no displacement, or force is perpendicular to displacement.

12. Energy  Energy is the capacity to do work.  SI unit: joule  Kinetic Energy  Energy possessed by an object because of its motion:  [  KE=\frac{1}{2}mv^2  ]  Potential Energy  Energy possessed by an object because of its position:  [  PE=mgh  ]  Law of Conservation of Energy  Energy can neither be created nor destroyed. It can only be converted from one form to another.  13. Power  Power is the rate at which work is done.  [  P=\frac{W}{t}  ]  SI unit: watt, or W  [  1W=1J/s  ]

14. Pressure  Pressure is the force acting per unit area.  [  P=\frac{F}{A}  ]  SI unit: pascal, or Pa  [  1Pa=1N/m^2  ]  Pressure increases when:  ●   Force increases  ●   Contact area decreases  15. Density  Density is the mass present per unit volume.  [  \rho=\frac{m}{V}  ]  SI unit: kg/m³  An object generally floats when its average density is less than the density of the liquid.  16. Heat and Temperature  Heat  Heat is energy transferred from a hotter object to a colder object.  SI unit: joule  Temperature  Temperature measures how hot or cold an object is.  Common units:

●   Degree Celsius: °C  ●   Kelvin: K  [  K=^\circ C+273  ]  Methods of Heat Transfer  1.   Conduction:   Transfer through direct contact.  2.   Convection:   Transfer through the movement of fluids.  3.   Radiation:   Transfer through electromagnetic waves.  17. Waves  A wave transfers energy from one place to another without permanently transferring matter.  Important terms:  ●   Amplitude:   Maximum displacement from the mean position.  ●   Wavelength:   Distance between two consecutive similar points.  ●   Frequency:   Number of oscillations per second.  ●   Time period:   Time taken for one oscillation.  [  f=\frac{1}{T}  ]  Wave speed:  [  v=f\lambda  ]  Where:  ●   (v) = wave speed  ●   (f) = frequency  ●   (\lambda) = wavelength  18. Light  Reflection

Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface.  Laws of reflection:  1.   Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.  2.   The incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.  Refraction  Refraction is the bending of light when it travels from one medium to another.  ●   Light bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium.  ●   Light bends away from the normal when entering a rarer medium.
